what_happened: Nobody owned onboarding for IdentityCo: sandbox access was requested only after the contract was signed in week 5, so integration testing started late; the sandbox outage (I001) then stopped it with no fallback
root_cause: The PMO standard plan template has no vendor onboarding workstream, so no owner, access lead times or test fallback were planned
evidence: SSO working in test reached on 2026-07-17, two weeks late; WBS 1.3.1 RED at month 3 (SPI 0.75, CPI 0.69); issue I001; post-mortem 2026-07-22
recommendation: Add a vendor onboarding workstream to the standard plan: a named owner from the day of award, access and environment lead times, and a stub for each external integration
applies_to: PMO standard plan template (vendor onboarding workstream)

what_happened: 1.3.1 was RED at the M2 close (2026-06-05: CPI 0.78, SPI 0.70), but the weekly status reports of 2026-06-12 and 2026-06-19 showed SSO AMBER without naming the threatened M4 pilot date; the sponsor learned of the threat only when it was escalated as DEC002 on 2026-06-26
root_cause: Weekly status rated dimensions only, so a RED work package from the monthly close never reached the sponsor, and an AMBER line did not have to name the milestone it threatened
evidence: M2 close 2026-06-05 (1.3.1 CPI 0.78; SPI 0.70); status reports of 2026-06-12 and 2026-06-19; escalation DEC002 on 2026-06-26; raised by Dana Okoro at steering on 2026-06-30
recommendation: Name every RED work package from the latest close, and the milestone any AMBER line threatens, in the weekly status report, and tell the sponsor the same day
applies_to: Helios status reports from 2026-07-03; PMO status-report standard

what_happened: Reusing a proven API design and its contract tests from an earlier project cut build time on the knowledge base (WBS 1.3.3)
root_cause: The design, contract tests and error-handling patterns were already proven, so no design spike was needed and integration defects were few
evidence: Month-3 earned value: knowledge base EV $33,000 against PV $30,000 and AC $30,000 (SPI 1.10, CPI 1.10), the only work package ahead of plan; M4 milestone review 2026-08-11
recommendation: Publish the API design and its contract tests as a reusable pattern and point new projects to it at design

what_happened: Testers and developers shared one QA environment; its data went stale and produced false test failures in the last week of sprint S4
root_cause: The plan provided a single non-production environment with no owner for test data, so nobody refreshed it between test cycles
evidence: Issue I003 (raised 2026-07-01); top-voted theme at the S4 retrospective
recommendation: Provide a dedicated test environment with a named owner and a data refresh before each test cycle, in place before system testing starts
applies_to: Issue I003 (Helios, before UAT starts on 2026-07-28); PMO test-strategy checklist

what_happened: Daily stand-ups drifted into problem-solving and ran over 30 minutes
root_cause: No agreed timebox or place for problem-solving, so every blocker was worked through in front of the whole team
evidence: S2 retrospective: stand-ups averaged 32 minutes over the sprint (team's own timing)
recommendation: Hold stand-ups to 15 minutes against the sprint goal and move problem-solving to a follow-on huddle of only the people needed
applies_to: Next sprint backlog (S3); Helios team working agreement
check_back_result: S3 retrospective: stand-ups averaged 14 minutes over S3 and follow-on huddles were used on 6 of 10 days; kept in the working agreement

what_happened: An explicit out-of-scope list in the charter (native mobile apps, live chat, back-office CRM changes) settled late scope requests quickly
root_cause: The exclusions were agreed with the sponsor before planning, so each request was tested against a signed list instead of argued
evidence: CR001 live chat ($60,000) deferred to phase 2 by Dana Okoro on 2026-06-16 citing the list; no scope dispute reached the steering committee
recommendation: Keep the explicit out-of-scope list a required charter element, signed by the sponsor
check_back_result: Charter template already requires the out-of-scope list; confirmed at the post-project review, no change needed

what_happened: Support-agent training ran as one wave that ended on 2026-09-11 with no catch-up session, so six agents on leave during the wave were still untrained at the GA go/no-go
root_cause: The plan scheduled end-user training as a single wave with no catch-up or attendance check before go-live, so any absence became a go-live risk
evidence: GA go/no-go 2026-09-30: 54 of 60 agents trained (adoption target T1); condition C1 gave the other six until 2026-10-06
recommendation: Plan a catch-up training session for absentees between the end of training and the go/no-go, and check trained numbers against the adoption target when training ends
